children: Silver Tiger Metals shares fell sharply Tuesday after the company said it plans to raise 87 million Canadian dollars ($62 million) by way of a bought deal financing to fund the higher cost of developing its silver-gold project in Mexico.

The company noted the costs to develop its El Tigre project in Sonora have increased by about $37 million to $124 million from its initial capital expenditure estimate. The company attributed the higher capital requirement for the project's Stockwork Zone to mining industry inflation over the past two years.
It also cited higher equipment contract pricing, as well as costs related to an expanded geotechnical scope that required more drilling on the property.

To fund the continued costs of the project, Silver Tiger said that it has entered into an agreement with a syndicate of underwriters to raise C$87 million, with the option of adding another C$13.1 million for a total of about C$100 million.
The company plans to use the funds towards exploration and development expenditures as well as for working capital and general corporate purposes, it said.
